l: Question Decomposition for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Question Decomposition for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Abstract
s: The unit concerns a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline designed to improve answers to multi-hop questions by using question decomposition and reranking. An LLM decomposes each original query into sub-questions, passages are retrieved for each sub-question, and the merged candidate pool is reranked before answer generation. The approach pairs an off-the-shelf cross-encoder reranker with LLM-driven question decomposition without extra training or specialized indexing. Evaluations on MultiHop-RAG and HotpotQA report gains of 36.7% in MRR@10 retrieval and 11.6% in F1 answer accuracy over standard RAG baselines.

s: Question decomposition uses an LLM to break an original query into sub-questions. It effectively assembles complementary documents when paired with passage retrieval and reranking.

s: The unit concerns a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline that combines question decomposition with reranking for multi-hop question answering. s: This unit evaluates QD+RR, RR, QD, and Naive RAG on retrieval, answer, supporting-fact, and joint metrics for MultiHop-RAG and HotpotQA. Question decomposition usually produces five subqueries, despite most questions requiring only two or three gold evidence sentences, and the number of subqueries has near-zero correlation with the number of gold evidences. s: The unit examines how LLM-based question decomposition and cross-encoder reranking affect retrieval-augmented generation for complex and multi-hop question answering. Across four system variants and two datasets, combining question decomposition with reranking produced the largest gains in retrieval and answer correctness without extra training or domain-specific tuning. Question decomposition broadened evidence coverage by creating focused sub-queries, while reranking promoted the most relevant passages. The approach adds computational overhead and can introduce noise when queries are already precise, motivating future work on conditional question decomposition and more efficient models.

l: Question Decomposition for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Question Decomposition for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Limitations
s: The limitations concern an approach for improving multi-hop retrieval through question decomposition and reranking. Question decomposition can hurt performance for specific queries, while subquery quality depends on prompt design and the underlying large language model. The approach also increases computational overhead, latency, GPU requirements, and pipeline complexity. Its gains depend on a strong, domain-aligned cross-encoder reranker, and its single-shot pipeline does not support iterative evidence-based retrieval.
